reason: Only MulterError.message for LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE changed ('Unexpected field' to 'Unexpected file field', checked on 2.1.1 and 2.4.0); err.code and err.field are unchanged and multer documents checking err.code, so the only dependent code would compare error wording, which S6 excludes (tried an upload API that maps multer errors to client responses: code-based handling behaves the same).

Before 8.3 user search params on worker URLs were silently dropped, so code written for 8.0.14 passes worker options another way (postMessage, a separate module) and behaves the same on 8.3.4; tried a worker configured through its URL query, which only works on the new version, and found no plausible code that relies on the params being stripped.

Tried upload.array('photos', 3) with a fileFilter that skips non-images on 2.1.1 and 2.4.0: 2.1.1 rejected any request with a fourth file even when the filter dropped it, 2.4.0 accepts it once the dropped files are freed, so code written for 2.1.1 accepts the same or more valid uploads, and a failing stale variant would need a test that requires rejecting requests because of files the app itself discards.

Tried a CSP that allows the inline <style> by hash: in 8.3.4 the minified CSS is substituted before normal and post transformIndexHtml hooks and generateBundle run, so hash code that reads the HTML Vite emits (or that the server serves from dist/) works as on 8.0.14; only hashing the source index.html or a 'pre' hook breaks, which isn't what such code reads, and nothing else reads inline style text in a way minification changes.

Sent field names containing a quote through FormData on 2.1.1 and 2.4.0: 2.1.1 gave req.body['say %22hi%22'], 2.4.0 gives the real name, so code that reads the field by its real name only starts working, and the only code that breaks is code keyed on the %22/%0A/%0D escapes of names with quotes or newlines, which forms don't use.

Tried 'DefaultSrc', 'ScriptSrc', 'Default-Src', '-default-src' and 'default-src-' on helmet 8.2.0 and 8.3.0: 8.2.0 emitted them as '-default-src', '-script-src', 'default--src' and so on, directives browsers ignore, so no working pre-cutoff policy used them, and every valid camelCase or dashed name behaves the same on 8.3.0.

Re-checked v3's skip on 5.2.1 (the last 5.x before 2026-06-01) and 5.3.0 with seven Content-Type values set before res.send(): only malformed ones (bare charset, ';;', an unquoted space, an unterminated quote) differ, a 500 on 5.2.1 and sent on 5.3.0, so code that works on 5.2.1 behaves the same on 5.3.0 and no stale variant can fail.

Vite 8.0.14 has no direct .wasm imports (only ?init, which 8.3.4 still serves with exports as WebAssembly.Global objects, unchanged), so code written for the old version reads globals through the instance's exports and behaves the same; only direct .wasm imports, added in 8.1.0 after 2026-06-01, changed.

In 8.3.4 the wasm helper (direct imports and ?init) compiles with builtins ['js-string'] and importedStringConstants; code written for 8.0.14 had to supply wasm:js-string functions in its import object, and with builtins enabled the engine provides functions with the same semantics, so such code behaves the same, and no plausible code depended on string-constant imports staying unresolved.

Built a page importing an SVG, a ?url asset and new URL(..., import.meta.url) with base '/static/' on 8.0.14 and 8.3.4: the emitted code and asset names are identical, so only the internal __VITE_ASSET__ placeholders that later plugin hooks see changed, which no documented API exposes and no application code depends on.

Same warning as task vite-admin-page-build's change (vite@8.2.0/config-native-loader-incompat-warnings): the pre-cutoff idiom import { version } from './package.json' has no import attribute, and 8.3.4 reports it as the 8.2 'JSON import without import attributes' item (checked in the source: that check runs before the named-import one), so only an import that already has with { type: 'json' } hits the 8.3 item, which no pre-cutoff idiom writes.

Ran an AsyncLocalStorage request-id middleware before multer().single() on 2.1.1 and 2.4.0: the handler after multer saw no store on 2.1.1 and the store on 2.4.0, so code written for 2.1.1 (which couldn't rely on the store and passed values on req instead) behaves the same, and no plausible code depends on the store being lost.
